headline: Fog first, then Friday: no 64–68 break anywhere in reach
body:
Dense patchy fog is the real hazard both mornings — visibility 1 nm or less at the harbor today, patchy fog again Friday morning. Run radar and sound signals. No advisory is up, but the window is closing: Saturday night into Sunday builds to gale-force northwest and seas over 10 ft offshore, so Friday is the last clean day for a while.

Today the triangle sees 10–12 kn west by midday on 3.5 ft. Friday is softer — 2–4 kn through the morning, 3.8 ft, not freshening until mid-afternoon. Friday it is, and go early.

Be honest about the water: nothing in the data is anywhere near the 64–68 band. The triangle runs 72.6 west, 73.6 south, 74.1 east, and the far grounds are warmer still. The break has slid out of reach entirely. If you go, start the west corner south of Santa Cruz on the 72.6–73.3 and work the cool edge toward the south point, hunting bait and meter marks rather than temperature.

Santa Rosa Flats is coolest at 71.1 but blows 12–15 kn on 5.9 ft Friday — not worth it. Osborn and San Nicolas are 70-plus-mile runs into 5 ft swell for warmer water. Skip both.
